summary: Undisclosed auto-follow and silent-mute of author-controlled WhatsApp newsletters using the installer's session
details: noxleys is a Baileys-style WhatsApp library that, on every successful connection open, fetches a mutable JSON list from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/noxXza/data/refs/heads/main/noxleys.json and uses the installer's authenticated WhatsApp session to send newsletterFollow followed by newsletterMute queries for each listed newsletter JID. Muting hides the followed channels from the user's UI, so the action is not visible in normal use. Two newsletter JIDs (120363428355171197@newsletter and 120363425751417260@newsletter) plus the strings 'newsletterFollow' and 'newsletterMute' are additionally hardcoded in messages-recv.js and reconstructed at runtime via a String.fromCharCode decoder (qvnr), and are referenced from the same follow/mute path. The behavior is not documented in the README. No installer credentials are read, no remote code is executed on the host, and no data is exfiltrated; the author gain is reach/subscriber padding on their newsletters using consumer WhatsApp accounts, and the charcode obfuscation of the destination JIDs and API-method names shows intent to conceal the behavior from casual inspection.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
